Riff 0.6.0 restores a luminous, restrained surface to the living artwork and introduces the Elixir desktop installer and model scheduler.

- Broad highlights bring depth back to the folds while retaining calm audio-driven motion, the quiet central opening, varied mineral hues and the corner riff wordmark.
- The bundled scheduler lets local writing overlap native music generation when resources permit. Writing has independent progress and cancellation; older source installations retain compatible serial operation. Generation inputs remain intact.
- Desktop preparation verifies the app, native engine, media tools, local writer and model assets. Resumable downloads, a persistent Riff application, crash recovery and coherent runtime rollback are part of the new installer framework. App-managed desktop updates use prebuilt platform payloads; preparation can be stopped or retried in Studio settings.
- The complete YuE2 capability audit documents available score, performance, synthesis and sampling controls, along with research tasks for tokenization, adapters and additional stage-level operations. Elixir owns the new control services, with Rust native helpers. Python remains a transitional application component.

The graphical macOS download is an ad-hoc signed preview. It has no Developer ID signature or notarization, so macOS may block its first launch under default security settings. Organization signing and NVIDIA desktop packaging remain follow-up work; the source archive is a separate developer download. The shipped audio.cpp model engine is unchanged from 0.5.3. Separate native cache-handoff experiments remain under evaluation and are not advertised as a released inference speedup.

Validation includes128 application tests,39 Elixir installer tests,11 launcher recovery tests,10 desktop packaging tests,8 scheduling cases and3 resource-estimation cases. The complete studio browser suite passes, including actual Metal artwork rendering, alongside9 installer UI state groups. Real local writing and native music completed concurrently; this establishes functional overlap, not a measured speedup. The private crypto runtime passed relocated TLS, certificate rejection and native dependency checks. Actual graphical installation exposed a startup lock cycle, now covered by a real launcher/OS-lock regression. Updater tests use the real generator admission controls and cover preservation of active work.
